title: Dave P
content: My NDE is not as long or as intense as others I am aware of. I remember being pushed deep underwater and knowing that it was going to be a long time before I could resurface to take my next breath. It was a very long time ago, and I do not really remember struggling for breath. The memory of the NDE seemed to overshadow any fight for life. My ex-girlfriend may have a different view, because I probably told her when I got back to the accommodation. I remember a kind of reckoning. It was a passage of images from my life. It was only fleeting, so I am still uncertain if it was real because it was so brief. Mind you, I was only 26. I remember being aware of a softly lit orb in the distance. It was not necessarily at the end of a tunnel, but I remember moving or being drawn toward it. It was dark at its perimeters, so the tunnel imagery kind of fits. I had an awareness that everything is connected, maybe by love. People, particularly, but also plants and even the earth are all one. I was imagining, thinking, and knowing all this while I was moving towards the orb. The orb seemed attractive and emanated calm, as if it was inevitable that I was going to be drawn to it. Then I popped up and took a breath, and everything I had experienced vanished. Now, having spent some time studying the phenomena, I recognize it as a shared consciousness, though I do not like to let experiences or learning after the NDE provide names or even interpret the experience. As I said, it was a long time ago. I may have forgotten the trauma of drowning, but the NDE experience has stayed with me. Embarrassingly, about six years later, I mentioned it in my wedding speech, as that was the closest thing I had experienced to the culmination of our humanity being together; that everything and everybody connected. I remember looking at the blank faces in the crowd as I spoke, so I gave up and did not really speak about it for years. Now I am tempted to look at our wedding video to see what I did say about the experience.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Yes, Drowning, Life threatening event, but not clinical death
elements.Did you feel separated from your body?: I lost awareness of my body
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: More consciousness and alertness than normal, I think the life review was so quick I was aware that 'seeing your life flash before your eyes' should have been more comprehensive. Then I was moving toward the orb of light. I am not certain my level of consciousness was greater. It was just that I realized at that point there was far more to my consciousness, and the consciousness of those around me, than I had previously expected.
elements.At what time during the experience were: When I was heading toward the light.
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Everything seemed to be happening at once; or time stopped or lost all meaning, I am not sure how time worked. I am not sure how long I was in the otherworldly realm, but it all appeared to happen really quickly, even though for me to wash up would have been longer than a few seconds.
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: My vision was focused on the direction I was heading, so probably a little myopic. That said, I passed the life review, or some of it, and it seemed very clear.
elements.Did you pass into or through a tunnel?: Uncertain, I was heading toward the warm orb, so I was probably myopic and became focused on the tunnel.
elements.Did you see, or feel surrounded by, a br: A light clearly of mystical or other-worldly origin
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Yes, My memory was that it was distant at first. It was like an old-school round headlight with a dim, but warm emittance. As I got closer it became clearer, but I did not get close enough for it to be bright or blinding.
elements.Did you seem to enter some other, uneart: Some unfamiliar and strange place, The movement toward the light and the calmness, which was not the fury of the ocean surrounding my body.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: Just surprise, like wow, this is amazing.
elements.Did you feel a sense of harmony or unity: I felt united or one with the world
elements.Did scenes from your past come back to y: It was so fleeting and I was surprised it happened so quickly. There was possibly a girl there that I had some connection to, and an old primary school friend, but I did not immediately recognize anyone.
elements.What was your religion prior to your exp: Christian- Protestant, Not connected at all, nor practising a faith. When asked, I would have described myself as Christian.
elements.What is your religion now?: Unaffiliated- Nothing in particular- Religious unaffiliated
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was both consistent and not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, I was very much a young physicalist, so it really challenged what I believed.
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes, I am a lot kinder to insignificant living things. Even worms and snails I disturb benefit from their interactions with me. I try to be compassionate to some humans who frustrate me, sometimes successfully. I look at my wife and family and just smile. They are the very embodiment of my love.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, Yes, the unity of all things became very apparent.
Yes, The very fact that I was going somewhere seems to confirm there is more to existence than this realm.
Yes, I realized that we are all connected by a sense of love.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: I always had the feeling that we were rushing around 'playing the game' and I did too. As a husband, a father, an employee, but it never sat well with me. I worked really hard at achieving all of the above, but now all that busyness has subsided I have time to reflect and research. I almost believe in panpsychism and now contemplate that we are living in a simulation.
elements.Have your relationships changed specific: Yes, I am less inclined to 'react' to inputs from other humans.
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Yes, It is difficult to express because it is experienced in another realm. I believe it is hard to articulate because nobody really knows it happened. They are busy with their own lives, so I have just kept quiet for 33 years and gotten on with life. Consequently, I am probably not practiced in articulating such an experience.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience as accurately as other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, I worry that it is distorted by time and my curiosity in other people's NDE experiences.
elements.Do you have any psychic, non-ordinary or: Uncertain, I sometimes wonder (and my wife genuinely believes) that I can predict outcomes way before they happen. She often says to me 'why don't you just tell me so I don't have to worry', but I always thought that everybody has the same premonitions, so mine are nothing special.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: Yes, I am going through what Alan Watts describes as the Dark Night of the Soul. That arises as I have given myself permission to believe in my NDE and consequently I will try to change my behaviors to be more present and forgiving when others tell me of their (what seems often trivial) concerns.
elements.Did you have any knowledge of near death: Uncertain, I had always wondered but assumed it would never happen to me. Twenty-seven-year-olds are invincible, right?
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, It is inconceivable that it didn't happen and it is so similar to so many other NDEs.
elements.Did the questions asked and information: Yes, They seemed to account for all of my fleeting experience.
